newsitem.title: USA: NASA to replace next U.S. astronaut heading for Mir.
newsitem.headline: NASA to replace next U.S. astronaut heading for Mir.

text.p: NASA astronaut Wendy Lawrence will not replace Michael Foale aboard the Russian space station Mir in September because she never underwent space walk training, NASA said on Wednesday.

Lawrence, a U.S. Navy commander, would still fly on the U.S. shuttle mission to pick up Foale, but her backup, Dr. David Wolf, was the NASA astronaut who would stay aboard Mir for the next long-duration stay, NASA spokeswoman Eileen Walsh said in a recorded broadcast from Johnson Space Centre.
She said the decision would be announced at a news conference on Thursday.
Walsh said Lawrence did not fit into the Orlon space suit used by Russian astronauts for space walks, while Wolf did.
CNN reported that Lawrence, who is 5'3" tall, was too short for the suit.
Walsh said the next shuttle flight to pick up Foale, originally scheduled for Sept. 20, might be delayed by about 10 days to give Wolf more time to complete space walk training.
Wolf had been scheduled for launch in January for the final long-duration increment aboard Mir.
Lawrence would continue training as Wolf's backup in case she was needed to stay aboard Mir after all, NASA said.

U.S. and Russian space officials decided that all three astronauts aboard Mir needed to be trained in space walking capabilities -- rather than two as planned -- in light of extensive needed efforts to repair the Spektr module damaged by a supply ship in a near-fatal crash on June 25.
Earlier in an interview from Star City, Russia, where she was training with two Russian cosmonauts, said she was looking forward to working on Mir but knew it would only happen if it were repaired.
"I've prepared for over a year and am very much looking forward to seeing Mir," she told reporters in fluent, though accented, Russian.
